name: Cais da Ribeira
short: Porto's historic riverside quay on the Douro, lined with 17th–18th-century arcaded houses; inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage list in 1996.
long: Ribeira is Porto's oldest riverside quarter and the heart of its historic centre. Tall, narrow houses with arcades, tiled roofs and azulejo façades step down to the water, while Praça da Ribeira forms the centre of the quarter. For centuries port wine was shipped from here, its barrels carried down the Douro on flat-bottomed rabelo boats. In 1996 Ribeira, together with the Dom Luís I Bridge, was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage list.
history:
Ribeira is Porto's oldest riverside quarter, grown around a deep-water harbour that gave the city and the country their name (Portus Cale). Trade between Porto and Gaia thrived here as early as the Middle Ages, and the Douro was the main route for wine, salt and goods.

The present character of the quarter took shape in the 17th and 18th centuries: tall, narrow houses with arcades on the ground floor, tiled roofs and façades covered in azulejo tiles. Praça da Ribeira, with its fountain and old riverside market, became the centre.

From the 18th century Ribeira was a hub of the port wine trade: barrels were loaded in its warehouses and on its quays and carried down the Douro on rabelo boats. Nearby, in Miragaia, stands the Church of São Pedro de Miragaia, one of the oldest in the city.

By the 20th century the quarter had grown poor and dilapidated, but restoration began in the second half of the century. In 1996 the historic centre of Porto, including Ribeira and the Dom Luís I Bridge, was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage list. Today it is the tourist heart of the city, with restaurants, a rabelo landing stage and pleasure boats.
facts: Porto's riverside quarter; inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage list in 1996.
17th–18th-century arcaded houses and azulejo façades define the quay.
Praça da Ribeira is the historic heart of the quarter, with its market and fountain.
For centuries port wine was shipped from here on flat-bottomed rabelo boats.
The Church of São Pedro de Miragaia, one of the city's oldest, stands nearby.
tip: Come early in the morning before the crowds: the arcades and coloured façades are best appreciated then. Pleasure boats leave from Praça da Ribeira, and the Gaia cable car runs nearby.
